title: Remote state, modules, capstone infrastructure
exp: Remote state is the first thing a real team adds. Modules scale beyond one file -- together they make a team-shared system.
pts: Remote backend (S3+DynamoDB): state in S3 (durable, encrypted); DynamoDB provides mutex preventing concurrent applies.
Module: reusable resource package. modules/s3-bucket/main.tf + variables.tf + outputs.tf.
terraform import: bring an existing resource under Terraform management without recreating it.
Sensitive variables: variable 'db_password' { sensitive = true } -- redacted from output.

viz.note: Two engineers both terraform apply -> DynamoDB lock table -> one gets lock -> applies -> releases -> second applies. No corruption.

qa.q: Why S3 + DynamoDB for remote state?
qa.a: S3 stores the file centrally, encrypted, with versioning. DynamoDB adds a mutex: before terraform apply, Terraform writes a lock entry; if another apply is running, it waits. Prevents concurrent applies from corrupting state -- essential for CI/CD and team use.

A reusable package of resources. Instead of copy-pasting the same S3+versioning+public-access-block setup every project, write once and call it. Enforces standards without remembering to add each resource manually every time.
